methodology: Flock Fantasy's Top 100 is the cross-position opinion anchor. The August 24 Top 50 WR ordering replaces the older relative WR order while preserving the Top 100's cross-position draft slots. Riser and faller videos are applied as modest, dated rank-point adjustments only after their underlying injury or depth-chart premise is checked against newer reporting. Every league then re-ranks the blended board using its scoring, team count, starter requirements, flex count and bench depth.

sources.title: 6 Players Falling Down my Fantasy Football Rankings

movementSignals.headline: Late-round volume route opened in Indianapolis
movementSignals.detail: Flock moved Allen to WR56 after Indianapolis signed him and the Colts' pass-catcher injuries created immediate opportunity.
movementSignals.verification: The Colts officially signed Allen on August 19; Tyler Warren remained out with a groin injury and Alec Pierce remained on Active/PUP as of August 23.

movementSignals.headline: Target concentration rose, then Houston added competition
movementSignals.detail: The Jayden Higgins ACL tear initially raised Collins' ceiling; the adjustment is deliberately small after Houston traded for Kayshon Boutte.
movementSignals.verification: Higgins is out for 2026, but Houston acquired Boutte on August 24.

movementSignals.headline: Late-round path reopened in Houston
movementSignals.detail: Flock moved Dell toward WR60 after Higgins' injury, while acknowledging a slow return and a wide range of outcomes.
movementSignals.verification: Higgins is out for the year; Boutte's arrival tempers Dell's opportunity gain.

movementSignals.headline: Early-season lead-work opportunity
movementSignals.detail: Flock moved Etienne into Round 3 after Alvin Kamara's MCL sprain.
movementSignals.verification: NFL.com reported Kamara is expected to miss at least one month and Etienne should receive the bulk of the reps.

movementSignals.headline: New Orleans target share strengthened
movementSignals.detail: Flock moved Olave to the late second/early third after Jordyn Tyson's renewed hamstring absence.
movementSignals.verification: NFL Network reported Tyson is expected to miss roughly two months.

movementSignals.headline: Fourth-round role confidence
movementSignals.detail: Flock raised Swift from a fifth-round value toward Round 4 on workload confidence.
movementSignals.verification: Applied as analyst opinion; no newer injury premise is required.

movementSignals.headline: Carolina rotation is creating a buy window
movementSignals.detail: Flock treated Brooks as a major riser and premium upside back rather than only a handcuff.
movementSignals.verification: Carolina lists Brooks second behind Chuba Hubbard and says it plans to rotate its backs; Hubbard is targeting Week 1 while recovering from a hamstring injury.

movementSignals.headline: Jacksonville role has expanded
movementSignals.detail: Flock highlighted Washington as a middle/late-round beneficiary in a changed Jaguars passing tree.
movementSignals.verification: Retained as a dated analyst movement signal, not an injury designation.

movementSignals.headline: Healthy-price upside remains
movementSignals.detail: Flock moved Godwin up as his current draft price continued to discount a meaningful Tampa Bay role.
movementSignals.verification: Tampa Bay still describes Godwin as a central slot weapon; the team also calls Emeka Egbuka week-to-week with a toe injury.

movementSignals.headline: Week 1 path improved after PUP activation
movementSignals.detail: Flock identified the discounted elite-TE ceiling, but the health layer remains cautious.
movementSignals.verification: San Francisco activated Kittle from PUP on August 23; he did individual work but not team drills while targeting a possible Week 1 return.

movementSignals.headline: Backfield became less clean
movementSignals.detail: Flock moved Skattebo toward the late fourth/early fifth after New York added Najee Harris and questioned Skattebo's rehab timetable.
movementSignals.verification: The Giants officially signed Harris on August 18; this is a role discount, not a claim that Skattebo lost the starting job.

movementSignals.headline: Crowded Giants backfield
movementSignals.detail: Flock moved Tracy into final-round territory after the Najee Harris addition.
movementSignals.verification: The Harris signing is official; Tracy remains rostered and the signal is a role/price warning.

movementSignals.headline: Third-round price discipline
movementSignals.detail: Flock moved Hall toward the end of Round 3 because his expected workload and team environment no longer supported the older premium.
movementSignals.verification: Applied as analyst valuation; no current injury penalty is added.

movementSignals.headline: High-ankle sprain adds early-season uncertainty
movementSignals.detail: Flock moved Love toward the middle of Round 3 before the latest Week 1 status update.
movementSignals.verification: Current reporting lists Love questionable for Week 1 after a high-ankle sprain and no more preseason action.

movementSignals.headline: Multi-week hamstring absence
movementSignals.detail: Flock pushed Tyson toward WR41 and made him an IR-slot-dependent pick.
movementSignals.verification: NFL Network reported an expected two-month absence; the injury model applies the separate availability penalty.

movementSignals.headline: Target competition exceeds the price
movementSignals.detail: Flock moved Downs outside the top 36 WRs after Indianapolis added Keenan Allen.
movementSignals.verification: Allen's signing is official; Warren and Pierce injuries are tracked separately rather than assumed permanent.

movementSignals.headline: Price and Active/PUP status both matter
movementSignals.detail: Flock moved Pierce outside the top 36 WRs before the latest Indianapolis update.
movementSignals.verification: Pierce remained on Active/PUP as of August 23; CBS still expects a Week 1 return, so the injury penalty is modest rather than a four-game assumption.

movementSignals.headline: Age-and-price decline signal
movementSignals.detail: Flock lowered Evans on role and trajectory rather than a current injury report.
movementSignals.verification: Applied only as analyst valuation; no injury tag is created.

movementSignals.headline: Workload confidence weakened
movementSignals.detail: Flock lowered Harvey after preseason usage created more competition than expected.
movementSignals.verification: Applied as a dated role/price signal, not as an injury report.

movementSignals.headline: Rotation risk increased
movementSignals.detail: Flock lowered Hubbard as Jonathon Brooks regained momentum.
movementSignals.verification: Carolina still lists Hubbard first, but explicitly plans to rotate the backs; Hubbard also remains out with a hamstring injury while targeting Week 1.

movementSignals.headline: Camp interruption, but not a full fade
movementSignals.detail: Flock initially lowered Lemon, then described him as a buy-the-dip once he returned; the model keeps only a small net downgrade.
movementSignals.verification: The contradictory movement is intentionally moderated rather than double-counted.
